data: Custom Transforms

**Trusted-input posture.** The dotted-path syntax causes Soup to import an
arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values
as *trusted input*: do not feed untrusted or operator-controlled YAML into ``soup
build`` on shared CI hosts. An attacker who controls the manifest can execute
arbitrary code during the build phase. If you must accept user-supplied manifests,
validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

performance-and-quantization: NF4 streaming (`quantization: 4bit`)

Pageable memory makes the host-to-device copy synchronous, which costs overlap — visible as the GPU-utilisation drop from 96.8% (1.5B, pinned) to 79.3% (3B, pageable).

Soup does this fallback automatically **and prints the cost** rather than absorbing it silently.

NF4 lifts this at 3B: the store drops under the ceiling and pins.

- Numbers are Windows/WDDM and therefore systematically pessimistic versus Linux.

`expandable_segments:True` is silently ignored on Windows; Soup detects that and does not claim it is active.

SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml

payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

commands: Fine-tune from your coding agent (MCP)

**Execution Security & Boundaries:**
- **Flag Safety:** `--allow-execute` is default-off and dangerous.

`--allow-mutating` alone can NEVER trigger subprocess execution.

- **One-Time Confirmation Tokens:** Authorization requires a server-issued random token.

Client confirmation is UX-only; security relies entirely on the server-side token state.

- **Subprocess Isolation:** Execution runs the Soup CLI as an isolated subprocess (`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `cwd` pinned to server startup directory).

Child stdout/stderr is redirected to `.soup/mcp-runs/<run_id>.log` to avoid corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stdio stream.

The frozen rule requires median reduction >= 2%, ordinary 95% and family 98.75% whole-pair bootstrap lower bounds above 0, exactness and the memory gate. 10000 resamples, seed 42. Five pairs give a small, discrete bootstrap sample; the bounds describe this experiment and do not guarantee population coverage. All four planned comparisons stay in the correction family.

See the [pre-timing protocol](protocol-2050-selective-checkpoint.md), [independent audit](results/issue2050-rtx3090-v1/independent-audit.json), [compact process evidence](results/issue2050-rtx3090-v1/process-evidence.json) and all four raw pair directories beside it. performance-and-quantization: NF4 streaming (`quantization: 4bit`)

Pageable memory makes the host-to-device copy synchronous, which costs overlap — visible as the GPU-utilisation drop from 96.8% (1.5B, pinned) to 79.3% (3B, pageable).

Soup does this fallback automatically **and prints the cost** rather than absorbing it silently.

NF4 lifts this at 3B: the store drops under the ceiling and pins.

- Numbers are Windows/WDDM and therefore systematically pessimistic versus Linux.

commands: Fine-tune from your coding agent (MCP)

**Execution Security & Boundaries:**
- **Flag Safety:** `--allow-execute` is default-off and dangerous.

`--allow-mutating` alone can NEVER trigger subprocess execution.

- **One-Time Confirmation Tokens:** Authorization requires a server-issued random token.

Client confirmation is UX-only; security relies entirely on the server-side token state.

- **Subprocess Isolation:** Execution runs the Soup CLI as an isolated subprocess (`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `cwd` pinned to server startup directory).

Child stdout/stderr is redirected to `.soup/mcp-runs/<run_id>.log` to avoid corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stdio stream.

data: Preference-Data Linter (`soup data lint`)

Five checks: `length_bias` — the **#1 silent DPO degradation**: `chosen`
systematically longer than `rejected`, reported as a Cohen's d effect size —
`label_imbalance` (KTO desirable:undesirable ratio), `near_duplicates`

`pip install "soup-cli[data]"`, degrades to an advisory skip otherwise),
`identical_pairs` (`chosen == rejected` — zero preference signal), and
`prompt_leak` (the prompt echoed verbatim inside the completion, a common
synthetic-data pipeline bug). Same OK/MINOR/MAJOR taxonomy and exit codes as
`soup data doctor`.

serving-and-export: HF Space SDK Auto-Pick

When you deploy a custom Space template directory, Soup now picks `space_sdk="streamlit"` / `"gradio"` from the rendered `requirements.txt`:

```bash
soup deploy hf-space --space my-org/my-app --model my-org/my-model --template-dir ./my-template
```

If `requirements.txt` lists `streamlit`, the Space is created with the Streamlit SDK. Otherwise (no requirements, gradio listed, etc.), Soup falls back to the Gradio default. The HF Hub allows `docker` and `static` SDKs too, but those cannot be inferred from `requirements.txt` alone — use the built-in templates or supply a custom one with an explicit `--sdk` override.

performance-and-quantization: NF4 streaming (`quantization: 4bit`)

Pageable memory makes the host-to-device copy synchronous, which costs overlap — visible as the GPU-utilisation drop from 96.8% (1.5B, pinned) to 79.3% (3B, pageable).

Soup does this fallback automatically **and prints the cost** rather than absorbing it silently.

NF4 lifts this at 3B: the store drops under the ceiling and pins.

- Numbers are Windows/WDDM and therefore systematically pessimistic versus Linux.

`expandable_segments:True` is silently ignored on Windows; Soup detects that and does not claim it is active.

**Webhooks (v0.71.5).** `soup ingest`, `soup prune-prompt`, `soup ab`, and `soup data active-sample` all accept `--slack-url` / `--discord-url` and POST a one-line summary on completion through the same SSRF-hardened validator as `soup drift-alarm` (scheme allowlist, loopback-only HTTP, RFC1918 / link-local / reserved / multicast rejected; the post never raises, so a flaky webhook can't fail the command). `soup ab` only fires when the sequential test actually decides (`reject_h0` / `accept_h0`), not while it's still `continue`-ing.

performance-and-quantization: NF4 streaming (`quantization: 4bit`)

Pageable memory makes the host-to-device copy synchronous, which costs overlap — visible as the GPU-utilisation drop from 96.8% (1.5B, pinned) to 79.3% (3B, pageable).

Soup does this fallback automatically **and prints the cost** rather than absorbing it silently.

NF4 lifts this at 3B: the store drops under the ceiling and pins.

- Numbers are Windows/WDDM and therefore systematically pessimistic versus Linux.

`expandable_segments:True` is silently ignored on Windows; Soup detects that and does not claim it is active.

training: Seeds & reproducibility (`training.seed`)

**Why you want this.** Without a seed knob every run of a config took the same
default, so "run it again with a different seed" was impossible: replicates of
one arm differed only by row permutation and GPU nondeterminism. That understates
run-to-run spread, and spread is the yardstick a real between-arm difference has
to beat. Three replicates at three seeds is the cheapest honest error bar you can
put on a training change:

```bash
for s in 1 2 3; do
  soup train --config soup.yaml --output "runs/seed-$s" \
    && echo "seed $s done"   # set training.seed: $s in the config per run
done
```

2329.changed

- **`soup serve` checks `--tool-auth-token` with the rule `soup ui` and `soup mcp serve` use**:
  16 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`.

A value from the option or from
  `SOUP_TOOL_AUTH_TOKEN` that does not match stops the command with exit 2 before the model
  loads, on every bind; the message names the rule, never the value.

The shared check now
  matches the whole value, so a valid token followed by a newline is refused by all three
  commands.

Upgrade note: a token shorter than 16 or longer than 128 characters, or with other
  characters, now stops `soup serve` at start; generate one with
  `python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"`.

data: Preference-Data Linter (`soup data lint`)

Five checks: `length_bias` — the **#1 silent DPO degradation**: `chosen`
systematically longer than `rejected`, reported as a Cohen's d effect size —
`label_imbalance` (KTO desirable:undesirable ratio), `near_duplicates`
(MinHash/LSH, reuses the `soup data dedup` kernel; requires
`pip install "soup-cli[data]"`, degrades to an advisory skip otherwise),
`identical_pairs` (`chosen == rejected` — zero preference signal), and
`prompt_leak` (the prompt echoed verbatim inside the completion, a common
synthetic-data pipeline bug). Same OK/MINOR/MAJOR taxonomy and exit codes as
`soup data doctor`.

pre-flight that budgeted only weights and buffers would wave that configuration through.

expects not to fit**:

- **`soup serve` checks `--tool-auth-token` with the rule `soup ui` and `soup mcp serve` use**:
  16 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`.

  commands.

  characters, now stops `soup serve` at start; generate one with
  `python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"`.

**Execution Security & Boundaries:**
- **Flag Safety:** `--allow-execute` is default-off and dangerous.

`--allow-mutating` alone can NEVER trigger subprocess execution.

- **One-Time Confirmation Tokens:** Authorization requires a server-issued random token.

Client confirmation is UX-only; security relies entirely on the server-side token state.

- **Subprocess Isolation:** Execution runs the Soup CLI as an isolated subprocess (`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `cwd` pinned to server startup directory).

Child stdout/stderr is redirected to `.soup/mcp-runs/<run_id>.log` to avoid corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stdio stream.

- **`soup profile --model` answers whether a model fits without a `soup.yaml`, and Apple Silicon is checked against Metal's working set (#2049 by @abdulwaarith0 in #2285).** `soup profile --model <id or directory>` prices the run set by `--seq`, `--batch`, `--method lora|qlora|full`, `--lora-r`, `--optimizer` and `--gradient-checkpointing`, with the same estimate and the same bytes as a `soup.yaml` describing that run.

It reads the model's `config.json` from a local directory, the Hugging Face cache or the Hub, so it works offline once the config is cached; when none can be read it exits 1 with the reason instead of pricing a shape guessed from the name.

**(d) `--control-sync-source`,** which is how the same-day control was made
without changing `src/`.

The runtime no longer constructs `DiskSource` for
`tier='disk'`, so the switch replaces the one name `_build_source` imports
lazily with a subclass of the shipped `DiskSource` that accepts and ignores the
two keyword arguments the async source added.

The buffer pool, the prefetcher
and the layer wrapper stay the shipped ones — exactly as before Task 5 — and
`_release_source` is duck-typed, so it is a no-op against a source with no
`release`.

The control therefore isolates the **read path**, not a different

performance-and-quantization: Gradient Checkpointing Tiers

Instead of a boolean, `gradient_checkpointing` now accepts a tier that trades compute for memory more precisely:

```yaml
training:
  # One of: false | true | "selective" | "medium" | "full" | "auto"
  gradient_checkpointing: auto
```

- **`full`** / `true` — every transformer block (~30% slowdown, biggest save).
- **`medium`** — every other block (balance).
- **`selective`** — attention only (~10% slowdown, modest save).
- **`auto`** — pick based on detected VRAM: < 24 GB → full, 24-80 GB → medium, > 80 GB → selective.

Legacy boolean configs continue to work unchanged.

backends-and-ops: Telemetry (opt-in)

Soup ships a hardware-info-only telemetry payload (Soup version + command +
Python major.minor + OS + arch + duration). It is **off by default** and never
sends model names, dataset paths, or config contents. Enable explicitly:

```bash
SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml
```

The PostHog network upload itself is deferred to v0.43.1; v0.43.0 ships the
payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

performance-and-quantization: Assistant-only loss masking

By default, Soup masks every non-assistant token with `-100` so the SFT loss reflects only what the model should *generate*. Toggle via `data.train_on_responses_only` (default `true`):

```yaml
data:
  train: data.jsonl
  train_on_responses_only: true   # default
  # OR per-message control:
  # train_on_messages_with_train_field: true
```

When the tokenizer ships a chat template with `{% generation %}` markers, the mask is exact. Without those markers, Soup falls back to an incremental tokenize-delta walk and documents the looseness.

data: Prompt Mining (`soup prune-prompt`)

Production LLM apps often pin a multi-paragraph system prompt to every request. Fine-tuning with that prefix wastes tokens (the model learns to copy what's already in context). `soup prune-prompt` finds the longest character prefix shared by ≥ 95% of rows and strips it, so the FT model internalises the behaviour instead.

```bash
soup prune-prompt --input traces.jsonl --output pruned.jsonl --min-frequency 0.95
```

Binary-search over up-to-32 candidate templates finds the longest qualifying prefix (a longer threshold-meeting prefix may exist beyond the universal one — Soup does not early-exit on the 100% match). Two-pass file read with a 100 000-row DoS cap.

data: Data Mixing Optimizer (BETA)

Writes a YAML recipe you can splice into your `soup.yaml`: `data.train` is the single highest-weighted dataset from the search (the full ranked weight/path breakdown is kept as a comment), and `data.interleave` carries the searched mixture weights but is not yet consumed by training — see the in-file comment, and #330/#443. `--budget` accepts `60s` / `5m` / `1h` / `24h`. ```bash
soup data mix --apply mix_recipe.yaml
```

data: Prompt Mining (`soup prune-prompt`)

Production LLM apps often pin a multi-paragraph system prompt to every request. Fine-tuning with that prefix wastes tokens (the model learns to copy what's already in context). `soup prune-prompt` finds the longest character prefix shared by ≥ 95% of rows and strips it, so the FT model internalises the behaviour instead.

```bash
soup prune-prompt --input traces.jsonl --output pruned.jsonl --min-frequency 0.95
```

Binary-search over up-to-32 candidate templates finds the longest qualifying prefix (a longer threshold-meeting prefix may exist beyond the universal one — Soup does not early-exit on the 100% match). Two-pass file read with a 100 000-row DoS cap.

commands: Fine-tune from your coding agent (MCP)

**Execution Security & Boundaries:**
- **Flag Safety:** `--allow-execute` is default-off and dangerous.

`--allow-mutating` alone can NEVER trigger subprocess execution.

- **One-Time Confirmation Tokens:** Authorization requires a server-issued random token.

Client confirmation is UX-only; security relies entirely on the server-side token state.

- **Subprocess Isolation:** Execution runs the Soup CLI as an isolated subprocess (`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `cwd` pinned to server startup directory).

Child stdout/stderr is redirected to `.soup/mcp-runs/<run_id>.log` to avoid corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stdio stream.

backends-and-ops: Telemetry (opt-in)

Soup ships a hardware-info-only telemetry payload (Soup version + command +
Python major.minor + OS + arch + duration). It is **off by default** and never
sends model names, dataset paths, or config contents. Enable explicitly:

```bash
SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml
```

The PostHog network upload itself is deferred to v0.43.1; v0.43.0 ships the
payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

**Roadmap:**

The cache is keyed to a fingerprint of the source checkpoint, so a base retrained in place re-shards instead of silently training against stale weights.

commands: Fine-tune from your coding agent (MCP)

**Execution Security & Boundaries:**
- **Flag Safety:** `--allow-execute` is default-off and dangerous.

`--allow-mutating` alone can NEVER trigger subprocess execution.

- **One-Time Confirmation Tokens:** Authorization requires a server-issued random token.

Client confirmation is UX-only; security relies entirely on the server-side token state.

- **Subprocess Isolation:** Execution runs the Soup CLI as an isolated subprocess (`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `cwd` pinned to server startup directory).

Child stdout/stderr is redirected to `.soup/mcp-runs/<run_id>.log` to avoid corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stdio stream.

data: Data Mixing Optimizer (BETA)

Writes a YAML recipe you can splice into your `soup.yaml`: `data.train` is the single highest-weighted dataset from the search (the full ranked weight/path breakdown is kept as a comment), and `data.interleave` carries the searched mixture weights but is not yet consumed by training — see the in-file comment, and #330/#443. `--budget` accepts `60s` / `5m` / `1h` / `24h`. Per-candidate proxy failures are isolated (DEBUG-logged, sentinel high loss recorded) so a single OOM combo does not abort the whole search; `partial=True` is surfaced in the report when the budget cap trips mid-loop.

Re-apply a previously written recipe:

```bash
soup data mix --apply mix_recipe.yaml
```

When training fails, Soup auto-writes a self-contained `.crash` JSON to
`./.soup-crashes/crash_<utc>_<hex>.crash` containing: redacted error trace,
classified failure kind (`oom` / `nan` / `cuda` / `dataloader` / `nccl` /
`other`), GPU state at crash time, env summary, last-50 metric rows, and the
config (recursively redacted of `hf_*` / `sk-*` / `Bearer …` tokens). The
output_dir is reduced to `os.path.basename` so `$HOME` doesn't leak.

data: Custom Transforms

**Trusted-input posture.** The dotted-path syntax causes Soup to import an
arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values
as *trusted input*: do not feed untrusted or operator-controlled YAML into ``soup
build`` on shared CI hosts. An attacker who controls the manifest can execute
arbitrary code during the build phase. If you must accept user-supplied manifests,
validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

**Webhooks (v0.71.5).** `soup ingest`, `soup prune-prompt`, `soup ab`, and `soup data active-sample` all accept `--slack-url` / `--discord-url` and POST a one-line summary on completion through the same SSRF-hardened validator as `soup drift-alarm` (scheme allowlist, loopback-only HTTP, RFC1918 / link-local / reserved / multicast rejected; the post never raises, so a flaky webhook can't fail the command). `soup ab` only fires when the sequential test actually decides (`reject_h0` / `accept_h0`), not while it's still `continue`-ing.

data: Prompt Mining (`soup prune-prompt`)

Production LLM apps often pin a multi-paragraph system prompt to every request. Fine-tuning with that prefix wastes tokens (the model learns to copy what's already in context). `soup prune-prompt` finds the longest character prefix shared by ≥ 95% of rows and strips it, so the FT model internalises the behaviour instead.

```bash
soup prune-prompt --input traces.jsonl --output pruned.jsonl --min-frequency 0.95
```

Binary-search over up-to-32 candidate templates finds the longest qualifying prefix (a longer threshold-meeting prefix may exist beyond the universal one — Soup does not early-exit on the 100% match). Two-pass file read with a 100 000-row DoS cap.

probe-v0.73.0-what-bounds-streaming: 3. Where the step actually goes (T1c)

CUDA-event instrumentation, `--mode events`. Two numbers matter and they are not
the same number:

- **copy time** — how long the transfers take on their own stream. Can overlap.
- **stall** — how long the *compute* stream sits blocked on a layer's copy
  event. This is the only part of the transfer that is **not** hidden.

Measured by recording an event on the compute stream immediately before and
after `wait_event`, so the gap between them is exactly the blocked interval.

backends-and-ops: Telemetry (opt-in)

Soup ships a hardware-info-only telemetry payload (Soup version + command +
Python major.minor + OS + arch + duration). It is **off by default** and never
sends model names, dataset paths, or config contents. Enable explicitly:

```bash
SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml
```

The PostHog network upload itself is deferred to v0.43.1; v0.43.0 ships the
payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

negative:
performance-and-quantization: Assistant-only loss masking

By default, Soup masks every non-assistant token with `-100` so the SFT loss reflects only what the model should *generate*. Toggle via `data.train_on_responses_only` (default `true`):

```yaml
data:
  train: data.jsonl
  train_on_responses_only: true   # default
  # OR per-message control:
  # train_on_messages_with_train_field: true
```

When the tokenizer ships a chat template with `{% generation %}` markers, the mask is exact. Without those markers, Soup falls back to an incremental tokenize-delta walk and documents the looseness.

negative:
performance-and-quantization: Live CUDA Batch-Size Probe

Set `auto_batch_size_strategy: probe` in `training:` and Soup will run a real OOM-probe before training:

```yaml
training:
  batch_size: auto
  auto_batch_size_strategy: probe
```

For each candidate size `B`, the probe runs ONE forward + backward + step on a synthetic batch of `B` sequences of length `max_length`. On `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` it halves; otherwise it doubles up to `4 × static_estimate`. The picked size is cached per `(model, max_length, quantization, lora_r, gpu)` tuple in `~/.soup/batch_cache.json` so subsequent runs skip the probe.

performance-and-quantization: Live CUDA Batch-Size Probe

Set `auto_batch_size_strategy: probe` in `training:` and Soup will run a real OOM-probe before training:

```yaml
training:
  batch_size: auto
  auto_batch_size_strategy: probe
```

For each candidate size `B`, the probe runs ONE forward + backward + step on a synthetic batch of `B` sequences of length `max_length`. On `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` it halves; otherwise it doubles up to `4 × static_estimate`. The picked size is cached per `(model, max_length, quantization, lora_r, gpu)` tuple in `~/.soup/batch_cache.json` so subsequent runs skip the probe.

data: Data Mixing Optimizer (BETA)

Writes a YAML recipe you can splice into your `soup.yaml`: `data.train` is the single highest-weighted dataset from the search (the full ranked weight/path breakdown is kept as a comment), and `data.interleave` carries the searched mixture weights but is not yet consumed by training — see the in-file comment, and #330/#443. `--budget` accepts `60s` / `5m` / `1h` / `24h`. Per-candidate proxy failures are isolated (DEBUG-logged, sentinel high loss recorded) so a single OOM combo does not abort the whole search; `partial=True` is surfaced in the report when the budget cap trips mid-loop.

Re-apply a previously written recipe:

```bash
soup data mix --apply mix_recipe.yaml
```

data: Preference-Data Linter (`soup data lint`)

Five checks: `length_bias` — the **#1 silent DPO degradation**: `chosen`
systematically longer than `rejected`, reported as a Cohen's d effect size —
`label_imbalance` (KTO desirable:undesirable ratio), `near_duplicates`
(MinHash/LSH, reuses the `soup data dedup` kernel; requires
`pip install "soup-cli[data]"`, degrades to an advisory skip otherwise),
`identical_pairs` (`chosen == rejected` — zero preference signal), and
`prompt_leak` (the prompt echoed verbatim inside the completion, a common
synthetic-data pipeline bug). Same OK/MINOR/MAJOR taxonomy and exit codes as
`soup data doctor`.

- The RAM store must be **allocated once and filled by `copy_`**, not
  `load_file -> .to() -> .pin_memory()`; the latter's 3 transient copies per
  layer are what push a large base over the page-locked ceiling.

- `expandable_segments:True` (plan P7) is **not supported on Windows** — torch
  warns and ignores it.

**Execution Security & Boundaries:**
- **Flag Safety:** `--allow-execute` is default-off and dangerous.

`--allow-mutating` alone can NEVER trigger subprocess execution.

- **One-Time Confirmation Tokens:** Authorization requires a server-issued random token.

Client confirmation is UX-only; security relies entirely on the server-side token state.

- **Subprocess Isolation:** Execution runs the Soup CLI as an isolated subprocess (`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `cwd` pinned to server startup directory).

Child stdout/stderr is redirected to `.soup/mcp-runs/<run_id>.log` to avoid corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stdio stream.

performance-and-quantization: Layer streaming is a CONFIG key, not a CLI flag — just train normally:

soup train --config soup.yaml
```

**How it works.** LoRA adapters + their gradients + optimizer state stay resident in VRAM (they are small). The frozen base lives in CPU RAM, page-locked when the machine allows it, and is streamed: each decoder layer is copied into one of two pre-allocated VRAM buffers on a dedicated CUDA stream while the previous layer is still computing, so the load overlaps the compute. Each layer is read **twice** per step — once in the forward pass and once when the backward pass recomputes it — because `dL/dx = Wᵀ · dL/dy` needs the weights to reach the layers below. That is physics, not an implementation detail, and it is why streaming costs time.

performance-and-quantization: Assistant-only loss masking

By default, Soup masks every non-assistant token with `-100` so the SFT loss reflects only what the model should *generate*. Toggle via `data.train_on_responses_only` (default `true`):

```yaml
data:
  train: data.jsonl
  train_on_responses_only: true   # default
  # OR per-message control:
  # train_on_messages_with_train_field: true
```

When the tokenizer ships a chat template with `{% generation %}` markers, the mask is exact. Without those markers, Soup falls back to an incremental tokenize-delta walk and documents the looseness.

the numbers above were taken):

  and `dL/dA` is structurally zero for *any* correct implementation. The first

  in checks 1 and 3.

  of the key-prefix bug below, leaving the models with different adapters. It
  now refuses to run rather than compare two differently-initialised models.

backends-and-ops: Telemetry (opt-in)

Soup ships a hardware-info-only telemetry payload (Soup version + command +
Python major.minor + OS + arch + duration). It is **off by default** and never
sends model names, dataset paths, or config contents. Enable explicitly:

```bash
SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml
```

The PostHog network upload itself is deferred to v0.43.1; v0.43.0 ships the
payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

data: Custom Transforms

**Trusted-input posture.** The dotted-path syntax causes Soup to import an
arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values
as *trusted input*: do not feed untrusted or operator-controlled YAML into ``soup
build`` on shared CI hosts. An attacker who controls the manifest can execute
arbitrary code during the build phase. If you must accept user-supplied manifests,
validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

negative:
training: Continual-learning rehearsal (`--replay`)

Fine-tuning on a new task can erase the old one. Rehearsal is the standard
defence: mix a slice of the old data back in.

```bash
soup train --config new_task.yaml --replay old_task.jsonl --replay-ratio 0.1
```

or in `soup.yaml`:

```yaml
data:
  train: new_task.jsonl
  replay: old_task.jsonl
  replay_ratio: 0.1      # fraction of the FINAL mixed set
  replay_seed: 0
```

**The ratio is a share of the final set**, not of the new data:

it only with the constant, the parameter accounting and the clock stated.**

as utilisation 79.3% -> 94.5%. This is the v0.72.0 honesty caveat #1 ("the 3B

backends-and-ops: Telemetry (opt-in)

Soup ships a hardware-info-only telemetry payload (Soup version + command +
Python major.minor + OS + arch + duration). It is **off by default** and never
sends model names, dataset paths, or config contents. Enable explicitly:

```bash
SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml
```

The PostHog network upload itself is deferred to v0.43.1; v0.43.0 ships the
payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values

validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

performance-and-quantization: Assistant-only loss masking

By default, Soup masks every non-assistant token with `-100` so the SFT loss reflects only what the model should *generate*. Toggle via `data.train_on_responses_only` (default `true`):

```yaml
data:
  train: data.jsonl
  train_on_responses_only: true   # default
  # OR per-message control:
  # train_on_messages_with_train_field: true
```

When the tokenizer ships a chat template with `{% generation %}` markers, the mask is exact. Without those markers, Soup falls back to an incremental tokenize-delta walk and documents the looseness.

serving-and-export: Inference Server Trace Log

`soup serve --trace-log <path>` writes a passive append-only JSONL log per chat completion:

```bash
soup serve --model ./out --trace-log ./serve-trace.jsonl --trace-log-cap-mb 100
```

Each line: `{"ts": ..., "prompt": ..., "response": ..., "latency_ms": ..., "tokens": ...}`. Path-containment validated, hard rotation cap (default 100 MB, one backup retained), symlink-reject on the backup path (TOCTOU defence), and `hf_*` / `sk-*` / `Bearer …` token shapes redacted to `<redacted>` before write. Failures (disk full, serialisation errors) never crash the request handler.

arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values

validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

performance-and-quantization: Sizing a streaming run (v0.72.3)

Streaming bounds the **weights**. It does nothing for activations or for the logits
tensor, and both scale with `batch × seq`. On a large-vocabulary model that second term
dominates everything else: measured on Qwen2.5-0.5B (vocab 151 936) at batch 8, S=512,
the logits alone are **8.71 GB — 146× the entire layer-buffer pool (0.060 GB)**. A
pre-flight that budgeted only weights and buffers would wave that configuration through.

So `soup train` predicts peak VRAM before building the model, and **refuses a run it
expects not to fit**:

**Execution Security & Boundaries:**
- **Flag Safety:** `--allow-execute` is default-off and dangerous.

`--allow-mutating` alone can NEVER trigger subprocess execution.

- **One-Time Confirmation Tokens:** Authorization requires a server-issued random token.

Client confirmation is UX-only; security relies entirely on the server-side token state.

- **Subprocess Isolation:** Execution runs the Soup CLI as an isolated subprocess (`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `cwd` pinned to server startup directory).

Child stdout/stderr is redirected to `.soup/mcp-runs/<run_id>.log` to avoid corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stdio stream.

performance-and-quantization: Live CUDA Batch-Size Probe

Set `auto_batch_size_strategy: probe` in `training:` and Soup will run a real OOM-probe before training:

```yaml
training:
  batch_size: auto
  auto_batch_size_strategy: probe
```

For each candidate size `B`, the probe runs ONE forward + backward + step on a synthetic batch of `B` sequences of length `max_length`. On `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` it halves; otherwise it doubles up to `4 × static_estimate`. The picked size is cached per `(model, max_length, quantization, lora_r, gpu)` tuple in `~/.soup/batch_cache.json` so subsequent runs skip the probe.

gate-v0.72.3-breadth: What the numbers actually say

3. **Accumulation's actual value under streaming is that it buys effective batch at
   constant VRAM**: peak moved 0.842 → 0.846 GB across accum 1→4, while reaching the same
   effective batch by raising batch cost 0.842 → 2.28 GB. So the guidance the pre-flight
   should give is: **raise `batch_size` until the VRAM pre-flight refuses, then use
   accumulation for the rest** — which is exactly the pairing this release now makes
   possible, since item 2 is what tells the user where that ceiling is.

4. Batch scaling is real but sub-linear: 556.6 → 1069.1 (1.92×) → 1378.0 (2.48×) for
   batch 1 → 2 → 4, as the run crosses from I/O-bound into compute-bound.

These are the working gate records written while the feature was built, not a

performance-and-quantization: Assistant-only loss masking

By default, Soup masks every non-assistant token with `-100` so the SFT loss reflects only what the model should *generate*. Toggle via `data.train_on_responses_only` (default `true`):

```yaml
data:
  train: data.jsonl
  train_on_responses_only: true   # default
  # OR per-message control:
  # train_on_messages_with_train_field: true
```

When the tokenizer ships a chat template with `{% generation %}` markers, the mask is exact. Without those markers, Soup falls back to an incremental tokenize-delta walk and documents the looseness.

Soup ships a hardware-info-only telemetry payload (Soup version + command +
Python major.minor + OS + arch + duration). It is **off by default** and never
sends model names, dataset paths, or config contents. Enable explicitly:

```bash
SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml
```

The PostHog network upload itself is deferred to v0.43.1; v0.43.0 ships the
payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

performance-and-quantization: Assistant-only loss masking

By default, Soup masks every non-assistant token with `-100` so the SFT loss reflects only what the model should *generate*. Toggle via `data.train_on_responses_only` (default `true`):

```yaml
data:
  train: data.jsonl
  train_on_responses_only: true   # default
  # OR per-message control:
  # train_on_messages_with_train_field: true
```

When the tokenizer ships a chat template with `{% generation %}` markers, the mask is exact. Without those markers, Soup falls back to an incremental tokenize-delta walk and documents the looseness.

anchor: How does Soup handle check loss curve in this workflow?
positive:
gate-v0.72.4-preference-losses: 1a — correctness battery, CPU float32, 4-layer Llama

**A3 is the check a loss curve cannot make.** The streamed layer substitutes base
weights through `functional_call` rather than the module's own `forward`, so
`disable_adapter()` being a no-op through that path is entirely plausible. If it
were, the reference would *be* the policy, every log-ratio would be 0, and the DPO
loss would sit at `−logsigmoid(0) = 0.6931` forever — which reads as "training
slowly", not as a bug. The zero-adapter control is what proves the 8.2e-01 gap
comes from the adapter and not from some other difference between the two forwards.

negative:
performance-and-quantization: Live CUDA Batch-Size Probe

Set `auto_batch_size_strategy: probe` in `training:` and Soup will run a real OOM-probe before training:

```yaml
training:
  batch_size: auto
  auto_batch_size_strategy: probe
```

For each candidate size `B`, the probe runs ONE forward + backward + step on a synthetic batch of `B` sequences of length `max_length`. On `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` it halves; otherwise it doubles up to `4 × static_estimate`. The picked size is cached per `(model, max_length, quantization, lora_r, gpu)` tuple in `~/.soup/batch_cache.json` so subsequent runs skip the probe.

performance-and-quantization: NF4 streaming (`quantization: 4bit`)

Pageable memory makes the host-to-device copy synchronous, which costs overlap — visible as the GPU-utilisation drop from 96.8% (1.5B, pinned) to 79.3% (3B, pageable).

Soup does this fallback automatically **and prints the cost** rather than absorbing it silently.

NF4 lifts this at 3B: the store drops under the ceiling and pins.

- Numbers are Windows/WDDM and therefore systematically pessimistic versus Linux.

`expandable_segments:True` is silently ignored on Windows; Soup detects that and does not claim it is active.

anchor: How does Soup handle shipped as-is because in this workflow?
positive:
gate-v0.72.4-preference-losses: The estimator is a sound UPPER bound for preference losses, and it is loose

```
seq  512  SFT 1.65 GB allowed  |  DPO 2.63 GB allowed
seq  768  SFT 2.14 GB allowed  |  DPO 3.60 GB REFUSED
seq 1024  SFT 2.63 GB allowed  |  DPO 4.58 GB REFUSED
```

The conservatism does **not** block the realistic seq-512 configuration; the exact
point where it starts refusing runs that would probably fit is **seq 768 at batch 1**.
Shipped as-is because under-predicting is the strictly worse failure — on Windows it
is not an exception but a silent WDDM spill — and documented rather than papered over.

anchor: How does Soup implement One CPU-only limitation, found by CI rather than locally in this configuration?
positive:
gate-v0.72.4-preference-losses: One CPU-only limitation, found by CI rather than locally

A full KTO **training step** over a streamed model runs on CUDA (verified here and
on the dev box) but fails on a CPU-only runner under newer torch/TRL with
`Tensor on device cpu is not on the expected device meta!`. Streaming exists to
bound VRAM, so a streamed model on CPU is a test convenience rather than a real
configuration — the same stance v0.72.3 took on PEFT's re-dispatch — and that test
is therefore gated to the production device. Everything else about KTO (the schema
gate, `setup()`, the reference behaviour, the layer-read accounting) is still
exercised on CPU.

Worth stating plainly: this was invisible on the dev box, which has CUDA. The
locally-green suite is a weaker signal than it looks whenever a code path forks on
device.

data: Custom Transforms

**Trusted-input posture.** The dotted-path syntax causes Soup to import an
arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values
as *trusted input*: do not feed untrusted or operator-controlled YAML into ``soup
build`` on shared CI hosts. An attacker who controls the manifest can execute
arbitrary code during the build phase. If you must accept user-supplied manifests,
validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

anchor: How does Soup implement 3. Where the step actually goes (T1c) in this configuration?
positive:
probe-v0.73.0-what-bounds-streaming: 3. Where the step actually goes (T1c)

CUDA-event instrumentation, `--mode events`. Two numbers matter and they are not
the same number:

- **copy time** — how long the transfers take on their own stream. Can overlap.
- **stall** — how long the *compute* stream sits blocked on a layer's copy
  event. This is the only part of the transfer that is **not** hidden.

Measured by recording an event on the compute stream immediately before and
after `wait_event`, so the gap between them is exactly the blocked interval.

Pageable memory makes the host-to-device copy synchronous, which costs overlap — visible as the GPU-utilisation drop from 96.8% (1.5B, pinned) to 79.3% (3B, pageable).

Soup does this fallback automatically **and prints the cost** rather than absorbing it silently.

NF4 lifts this at 3B: the store drops under the ceiling and pins.

data: Data Mixing Optimizer (BETA)

Writes a YAML recipe you can splice into your `soup.yaml`: `data.train` is the single highest-weighted dataset from the search (the full ranked weight/path breakdown is kept as a comment), and `data.interleave` carries the searched mixture weights but is not yet consumed by training — see the in-file comment, and #330/#443. `--budget` accepts `60s` / `5m` / `1h` / `24h`. Per-candidate proxy failures are isolated (DEBUG-logged, sentinel high loss recorded) so a single OOM combo does not abort the whole search; `partial=True` is surfaced in the report when the budget cap trips mid-loop.

Re-apply a previously written recipe:

```bash
soup data mix --apply mix_recipe.yaml
```

positive:
probe-v0.73.0-what-bounds-streaming: The control that decides how to read the CCE row

**Finding 8b — this is the part with a cost.** Soup's central claim, and the
criterion its CI enforces, is bit-exactness against a resident reference. Turning
CCE on **destroys that criterion**, and not because of streaming: a resident run
is not reproducible against *itself*. Any future release that ships
`use_cut_ce` with streaming has to replace "bit-exact" with "within the loss
kernel's measured noise floor", and has to measure that floor per model and per
shape. That is a strictly weaker guarantee than the one the project currently
makes, and it should be a deliberate decision rather than a side effect of
setting a flag.

anchor: How does Soup handle equal batch, saves in this workflow?
positive:
probe-v0.73.0-what-bounds-streaming: 9a. The headline: memory, not speed

- **At equal batch, CCE saves 0.304 GB (−8.8%) at b=1.** That is the whole of
  the answer to "measure peak VRAM in both cases" — and on its own it is not very
  interesting.

- **The slope is the interesting part, and it is dead linear.** Peak grows by
  **1.063 GB per extra microbatch** without CCE (1.064, 1.061) and by
  **0.319 GB** with it (0.319, 0.319) — a **3.33x** reduction in the marginal
  cost of a microbatch.

- The difference, **0.744 GB per 512 tokens**, is the cross-entropy pipeline:
  **11.32 bytes per logit element**.

there is nothing else for batching to recover.

positive:
probe-v0.73.0-what-bounds-streaming: 9c. Three things went wrong measuring this, all recorded

1.

**The first sweep ran ~20 minutes and left nothing.** The process died (exit
   4) with an empty log; results were only written at the end.

Fixed by
   persisting after every point — which is the only reason the data above
   survived the second crash.

2.

**A hard `CUDA error: out of memory` is not the allocator's
   `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError`.** It poisons the CUDA context, so every later
   call in that process fails; the `hf b=4` row killed the run and the remaining
   points had to be re-measured in a fresh process.

A sweep that walks a batch
   size upward past the refusal point must expect to be restarted, not to
   continue.

3.
negative:
2329.changed

- **`soup serve` checks `--tool-auth-token` with the rule `soup ui` and `soup mcp serve` use**:
  16 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`.

A value from the option or from
  `SOUP_TOOL_AUTH_TOKEN` that does not match stops the command with exit 2 before the model
  loads, on every bind; the message names the rule, never the value.

The shared check now
  matches the whole value, so a valid token followed by a newline is refused by all three
  commands.

Upgrade note: a token shorter than 16 or longer than 128 characters, or with other
  characters, now stops `soup serve` at start; generate one with
  `python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"`.

commands: Fine-tune from your coding agent (MCP)

**Execution Security & Boundaries:**
- **Flag Safety:** `--allow-execute` is default-off and dangerous.

`--allow-mutating` alone can NEVER trigger subprocess execution.

- **One-Time Confirmation Tokens:** Authorization requires a server-issued random token.

Client confirmation is UX-only; security relies entirely on the server-side token state.

- **Subprocess Isolation:** Execution runs the Soup CLI as an isolated subprocess (`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, `cwd` pinned to server startup directory).

Child stdout/stderr is redirected to `.soup/mcp-runs/<run_id>.log` to avoid corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stdio stream.

**Trusted-input posture.** The dotted-path syntax causes Soup to import an
arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values
as *trusted input*: do not feed untrusted or operator-controlled YAML into ``soup
build`` on shared CI hosts. An attacker who controls the manifest can execute
arbitrary code during the build phase. If you must accept user-supplied manifests,
validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

establishes that `MLXSFTTrainerWrapper`'s training loop runs end to end against a

adapters beyond "they load and the loss falls" — see *What this does not
establish*, which is longer than the results on purpose.

asked for exactly this and had been open since v0.25.0 because CI has no Apple
Silicon and the maintainer has no Mac.

arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values

build`` on shared CI hosts. An attacker who controls the manifest can execute
arbitrary code during the build phase. If you must accept user-supplied manifests,
validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

anchor: How does Soup handle interesting mechanism model in this workflow?
positive:
run-m1-8gb-mlx-sft: Host behaviour

The interesting mechanism is that **a model too big for RAM does not fail here —
it pages.** macOS grew the swap file through the run (2048 -> 3072 -> 4096 ->
8192 -> 9216 MB) and free memory sat at 5-6% for long stretches while `ls /`
still returned in 16 ms. MLX memory-maps weights, so most of the model is
file-backed and evictable; low "free memory" is the normal shape of this
workload, not distress.

anchor: How does Soup handle correctness claim. loss in this workflow?
positive:
run-m1-8gb-mlx-sft: What this does not establish

- **No correctness claim.** Loss falls and the adapter reloads.

Nothing here
  compares MLX output against a transformers reference, checks gradient
  exactness, or evaluates the tuned model.

"It trains" is the claim; "it trains
  *correctly*" is not.

- **The data is synthetic and trivial** — 48 rows of short Q/A, deliberately
  repetitive.

A loss falling from 3.6 to 0.1 on 48 repeated rows is memorisation,
  not evidence of learning.

It is a smoke signal, nothing more.

- **`target_modules: auto` means Q/V only here.** Every run printed
  `auto cannot be resolved for all architectures; defaulting to
  ['self_attn.q_proj', 'self_attn.v_proj']`.
negative:
performance-and-quantization: Assistant-only loss masking

By default, Soup masks every non-assistant token with `-100` so the SFT loss reflects only what the model should *generate*. Toggle via `data.train_on_responses_only` (default `true`):

```yaml
data:
  train: data.jsonl
  train_on_responses_only: true   # default
  # OR per-message control:
  # train_on_messages_with_train_field: true
```

When the tokenizer ships a chat template with `{% generation %}` markers, the mask is exact. Without those markers, Soup falls back to an incremental tokenize-delta walk and documents the looseness.

training: Continual-learning rehearsal (`--replay`)

Fine-tuning on a new task can erase the old one. Rehearsal is the standard
defence: mix a slice of the old data back in.

```bash
soup train --config new_task.yaml --replay old_task.jsonl --replay-ratio 0.1
```

or in `soup.yaml`:

```yaml
data:
  train: new_task.jsonl
  replay: old_task.jsonl
  replay_ratio: 0.1      # fraction of the FINAL mixed set
  replay_seed: 0
```

**The ratio is a share of the final set**, not of the new data:
`n_replay = round(r/(1-r) · n_new)`. At `0.1` over 1000 new rows that is 111
replay rows → 1111 total → exactly 10%. The console reports what it did:

--tracker mlflow requires the 'mlflow' package. Install with: pip install soup-cli[trackers] (or pip install mlflow)

pip install soup-cli[trackers]   # mlflow + swanlab + trackio

run-t4-colab-free-tier: An 8B streamed run on a free-tier Colab T4

**Status: RUN COMPLETED. Correctness NOT gated — see "What this does not
establish", which is longer than the results section on purpose.**

Every layer-streaming number this project has published came from one of two
machines: the maintainer's RTX 3050 Laptop (4 GB, Ampere, Windows) or a borrowed
8×H100 (Ampere-successor, Ubuntu). Both are Ampere or newer. The pre-Ampere fix
in #385/#387 was verified *using* fp16 **on an Ampere card**, which establishes
the plumbing and says nothing about Turing kernels — bitsandbytes NF4 on sm_75
in particular.

This run closes exactly that gap and nothing wider: **the code path runs to
completion on a Turing card.** It is the first streaming result from hardware the
maintainer does not own.

That the layer-streaming path — NF4 sharding, the pinned host store, the
two-buffer pool, fp16 compute selection after #385/#387 — **executes end to end
on a pre-Ampere card and writes a live adapter**, at an 8B model size, inside a
4 GB process budget. Before this, that had never been run.

arbitrary Python module and call a function from it. Treat ``transform`` values

validate them against a allowlist of permitted transform paths before passing
them to the resolver.

Streaming bounds the **weights**. It does nothing for activations or for the logits
tensor, and both scale with `batch × seq`. On a large-vocabulary model that second term
dominates everything else: measured on Qwen2.5-0.5B (vocab 151 936) at batch 8, S=512,
the logits alone are **8.71 GB — 146× the entire layer-buffer pool (0.060 GB)**. A
pre-flight that budgeted only weights and buffers would wave that configuration through.

So `soup train` predicts peak VRAM before building the model, and **refuses a run it
expects not to fit**:

**Two fixes from #2215 were applied at launch.** 0.77.0's `bench train` cannot
run any 4-bit config: TRL casts the adapters to bf16, the fingerprint hashed
them through numpy, and on an fp16 card it skipped the fp32 cast `soup train`
makes before training. The harness applied the two fixes from #2216 (a
byte-level fingerprint, and the same `align_trainable_dtype_for_fp16` call
`soup train` makes) only after checking that the installed release lacked each
one, and the first line of every log records it. The fingerprint is taken
before the first step and after the last, outside the timed window. With the
alignment, the adapters train in fp32, as they do under `soup train`.

performance-and-quantization: Preference losses over streaming (v0.72.4)

**Roadmap:**
- A published 14B-on-8 GB reference benchmark — hardware-blocked; it needs an 8 GB card and 32 GB of RAM, which the development box does not have
- GRPO and PPO are explicitly **not** planned: rollouts need generation, which re-reads the model per token

The cache is keyed to a fingerprint of the source checkpoint, so a base retrained in place re-shards instead of silently training against stale weights.

SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml

payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

performance-and-quantization: NF4 streaming (`quantization: 4bit`)

Pageable memory makes the host-to-device copy synchronous, which costs overlap — visible as the GPU-utilisation drop from 96.8% (1.5B, pinned) to 79.3% (3B, pageable).

Soup does this fallback automatically **and prints the cost** rather than absorbing it silently.

NF4 lifts this at 3B: the store drops under the ceiling and pins.

- Numbers are Windows/WDDM and therefore systematically pessimistic versus Linux.

`expandable_segments:True` is silently ignored on Windows; Soup detects that and does not claim it is active.

Soup ships a hardware-info-only telemetry payload (Soup version + command +
Python major.minor + OS + arch + duration). It is **off by default** and never
sends model names, dataset paths, or config contents. Enable explicitly:

```bash
SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml

The PostHog network upload itself is deferred to v0.43.1; v0.43.0 ships the
payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

```yaml
data:

When the tokenizer ships a chat template with `{% generation %}` markers, the mask is exact. Without those markers, Soup falls back to an incremental tokenize-delta walk and documents the looseness.

anchor: How does Soup execute 2185.fixed in this configuration?
positive:
2185.fixed

The input check now pre-parses the file: every loader failure — a suffix that is not `.jsonl`, an invalid JSON line, a row without `prompt`, a file with no tasks, and a file over `MAX_EVAL_TASKS`, plus any `OSError` or `ValueError` edge (`FileNotFoundError`, a path that exists but cannot be read, a decoding failure) — prints the loader's own message through `for_terminal` and exits 3, exactly like the already-refused missing file, so the mistake no longer costs the full model load.

The pre-parsed list is also handed to `run_quant_check`, whose command path no longer reads the file once per model; its existing `tasks_file` parameter keeps working for other callers and `soup eval custom` is deliberately untouched, as the issue scopes.

anchor: What does the `soup profile --json` command do?
positive:
2285.added

`--model` with `--config`, the run flags without `--model`, and `--lora-r` with `--method full` are refused.

On Apple Silicon, `soup profile` and the MCP `profile` tool now compare the estimate to Metal's recommended working-set size from mlx, not the whole unified memory, and report the memory as assumed when mlx cannot read it.

The `soup train` pre-flight still skips `backend: mlx`.

2329.changed

backends-and-ops: Telemetry (opt-in)

Soup ships a hardware-info-only telemetry payload (Soup version + command +
Python major.minor + OS + arch + duration). It is **off by default** and never
sends model names, dataset paths, or config contents. Enable explicitly:

```bash
SOUP_TELEMETRY=1 soup train --config soup.yaml
```

The PostHog network upload itself is deferred to v0.43.1; v0.43.0 ships the
payload schema only so you can audit it before opting in.

positive:
2372.fixed

anchor: How does Soup handle forward without argument in this workflow?
positive:
2372.fixed

A forward without the argument keeps the old call.

The VRAM estimate behind the `soup train` pre-flight, `soup profile`, `soup plan` and the MCP `profile` tool charges a PRM step's `logits` term on one position, `vocab × batch × 6` bytes, except for the eight causal-LM model types whose forward has no `logits_to_keep` (`gemma4_assistant`, `gemma4_unified_assistant`, `musicgen`, `musicgen_melody`, `prophetnet`, `trocr`, `whisper`, `xlstm`) and remote-code bases (`auto_map` in `config.json`), which keep the full-sequence charge.

anchor: How does Soup handle grpo trains pre-quantized in this workflow?
positive:
2386.added

- **MLX GRPO trains on pre-quantized 4-bit bases (#1976 by @ybai08 in #2386).** `task: grpo` with
  `backend: mlx` refused any base that loaded quantized.

It now also trains on a base
  pre-quantized by mlx-lm at 4 bits in `affine` mode, as `mlx_lm.convert -q` and the
  `mlx-community/...-4bit` repos write it, with the same loop and objective as on a dense
  base.

The quantized `QuantizedLinear` and `QuantizedEmbedding` layers (a tied output head
  included) stay frozen and only the LoRA adapter trains; a quantized tensor left trainable is
  refused before the first update, and the reference is the same quantized base with the
  adapter off.
negative:
training: PRM-guided GRPO (process-supervised RL)

```yaml
task: grpo
backend: transformers        # required (the PRM reward runs a transformers forward)
modality: text               # required
data:
  format: chatml
  train: ./grpo_prompts.jsonl
training:
  prm_reward: ./my-prm       # a `soup train task=prm` checkpoint dir (or HF id)
  prm_aggregate: min         # weakest-link (default) | prod | last
  num_generations: 4
  grpo_beta: 0.04
```

`prm_aggregate='min'` (weakest-link, the standard PRM aggregation) is the safe
default; `prod` assumes calibrated `[0,1]` step scores (Soup's PRM head is
trained with unconstrained MSE, so `prod` can blow up on uncalibrated labels).

anchor: How does Soup handle other quantized base in this workflow?
positive:
2386.added

Any other quantized base is refused right after the load, naming the first
  layer outside the rule with its bits and mode: 8-bit and mixed-bit recipes, `mxfp4`,
  `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`, quantized MoE layers and BitNet `BitLinear` layers.

`quantization: 8bit` stays refused at load.

`adapter_config.json` records the base's quantization as `base_quantization` (bits, group
  size, mode and the number of quantized linear and embedding layers; `null` for a dense
  base).

Try: `soup train --config soup.yaml` with `task: grpo`, `backend: mlx`,
  `quantization: 4bit` and a `mlx-community/...-4bit` base.

positive:
README: Changelog fragments

User-visible pull requests add one Markdown fragment instead of editing the shared
`CHANGELOG.md` file:

```text
changelog.d/<latest-release>/<number>.<category>.md
```

`<latest-release>` is the newest released version heading in `CHANGELOG.md`. `<number>`
should be the pull-request number rather than the issue it closes; this keeps two pull
requests for the same issue distinct and traceable. The validator rejects a second
category with the same number. `<category>` is one of `added`, `changed`, `deprecated`,
`removed`, `fixed`, or `security`.

data: Prompt Mining (`soup prune-prompt`)

Production LLM apps often pin a multi-paragraph system prompt to every request. Fine-tuning with that prefix wastes tokens (the model learns to copy what's already in context). `soup prune-prompt` finds the longest character prefix shared by ≥ 95% of rows and strips it, so the FT model internalises the behaviour instead.

```bash
soup prune-prompt --input traces.jsonl --output pruned.jsonl --min-frequency 0.95
```

Binary-search over up-to-32 candidate templates finds the longest qualifying prefix (a longer threshold-meeting prefix may exist beyond the universal one — Soup does not early-exit on the 100% match). Two-pass file read with a 100 000-row DoS cap.

serving-and-export: Cap the sequence length when the KV cache does not fit

soup serve --model ./output --backend vllm --max-model-len 8192
```

> **Tip:** Soup auto-detects vLLM. When installed, you'll see a hint during `soup serve` if you haven't enabled it yet.

The vLLM backend applies the **model's own chat template**, exactly like the
transformers backend — both call one shared prompt builder. A model that ships
no chat template falls back to a generic `User:` / `Assistant:` prompt, and the
server says so at startup. `finish_reason` reports `"length"` when a response
hits `max_tokens` and `"stop"` otherwise (`/v1/messages` maps those to
`max_tokens` / `end_turn`).
